g.text: HIGH APSEC-AUTH-002 State-changing operation is unauthenticated
DELETE /pets/{petId} changes state but has no effective security requirement.
Unauthenticated writes are a common path to data tampering and abuse.
fix: Attach a 'security' requirement to this operation, or confirm and document why it
HIGH APSEC-AUTH-002 State-changing operation is unauthenticated
POST /pets changes state but has no effective security requirement. Unauthenticated writes
are a common path to data tampering and abuse.
fix: Attach a 'security' requirement to this operation, or confirm and document why it
HIGH APSEC-TLS-001 Server declared over plaintext HTTP
The server URL 'http://api.petstore.example.com/v1' uses http://. Traffic — including
credentials and tokens — travels unencrypted and is open to interception and tampering.
fix: Serve the API exclusively over https:// and enable HSTS.
Security schemes exist but no top-level 'security' is set, so protection depends entirely
on per-operation overrides. A single missing override silently exposes an endpoint.
fix: Apply a default 'security' at the document root and relax it only on the specific
MEDIUM APSEC-AUTH-003 API key in query string ('apiKeyQuery')
API keys passed as query parameters leak into server logs, browser history and referer
fix: Send API keys in a header, not the query string.
MEDIUM APSEC-AUTH-003 HTTP Basic auth scheme 'basicAuth'
HTTP Basic transmits base64-encoded credentials on every request. Without strict TLS it is
trivially decodable and offers no token rotation or scoping.
fix: Prefer short-lived bearer tokens (OAuth2/JWT). If Basic is unavoidable, enforce TLS
